exercises.title: U1 听力·对话 Choosing a Sci-Fi Film
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Mia: There's a science fiction film festival this weekend. Want to go, Sam?
Sam: Sounds great. What films are they showing?
Mia: On Saturday it's a story about robots that take over a city.
Sam: Hmm, that sounds a bit scary. What about Sunday?
Mia: Sunday is about a girl who builds a time machine and travels to the future.
Sam: I love time-travel stories. Let's go on Sunday, then.
Mia: Perfect. I'll book two tickets online tonight.
Sam: Thanks. Shall we meet at the cinema at two o'clock?
exercises.translation_cn: Mia 邀 Sam 周末去科幻电影节;周六放机器人占领城市的片子,Sam 觉得有点吓人;周日放一个女孩造时间机器去未来的故事;Sam 爱看时间旅行,决定周日去;Mia 今晚网上订两张票,约定两点在影院碰面。

questions.stem: What event are Mia and Sam talking about?
What is Saturday's film about?
options: A girl and a time machine.

questions.stem: Why does Sam choose the Sunday film?
How will Mia get the tickets?
options: She will buy them at the door.

questions.stem: When will they meet at the cinema?

exercises.title: U1 听力·短文 What Is Science Fiction
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Science fiction is a kind of story about the future and about science.
It often describes robots, space travel, time machines, and life on other planets.
Long ago, robots existed only in such stories.
Today many of those imagined ideas are slowly becoming real.
Good science fiction makes us think about how technology may change our lives.
exercises.translation_cn: 科幻是一种关于未来和科学的故事;常描写机器人、太空旅行、时间机器和其他星球上的生活;很久以前,机器人只存在于这类故事中;如今许多想象中的点子正慢慢变成现实;好的科幻让我们思考科技会如何改变生活。

questions.stem: What is science fiction mainly about?
Which of these does science fiction often describe?
Where did robots exist long ago?
What is happening to many imagined ideas today?
What does good science fiction make us do?
options: Think about how technology may change life.

exercises.title: U1 听力·对话 An Interview with a Sci-Fi Expert
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Host: Welcome. You are an expert in science fiction. Do you have robots at home?
Expert: Yes, I have two. One helps me cook, and the other cleans the floor.
Host: Interesting! What jobs do you think robots will do in the future?
Expert: I believe they will work in teaching and nursing, helping people every day.
Host: That sounds useful. But could robots also become dangerous?
Expert: As they grow more intelligent, they may also become harder to control.
Host: So the line between humans and robots will get blurred?
Expert: Exactly. That is why clear rules and careful testing matter so much.
exercises.translation_cn: 主持人欢迎科幻专家,问他家里有没有机器人;专家有两个,一个帮做饭一个扫地;谈到未来机器人会从事教学和护理;主持人担心机器人也会变危险;专家说它们越聪明越难控制;人机界限会变模糊;因此明确规则和谨慎测试很重要。

questions.stem: How many robots does the expert have at home?
What does one of his robots do?
In which jobs does the expert think robots will work?
Why might robots become dangerous?
options: They grow more intelligent and harder to control.

questions.stem: What does the expert say matters so much?

exercises.title: U1 听力·短文 The Three Laws of Robotics
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: The famous writer Isaac Asimov created three laws to keep robots safe.
The first law says a robot must never harm a human being.
The second law says a robot must obey the orders given by people.
But it must not obey an order if that order breaks the first law.
The third law says a robot must protect itself, as long as this does not break the other laws.
exercises.translation_cn: 著名作家阿西莫夫制定了三条让机器人安全的定律;第一定律:机器人绝不能伤害人类;第二定律:机器人必须服从人的命令;但若命令违反第一定律则不可服从;第三定律:机器人必须保护自己,只要不违反前两条。

questions.stem: Who created the three laws of robotics?
What does the first law say a robot must never do?
What does the second law tell a robot to do?
options: Obey the orders given by people.

questions.stem: When must a robot not obey an order?
options: When the order breaks the first law.

questions.stem: What does the third law allow a robot to do?
options: Protect itself, if it breaks no other law.

exercises.title: U1 听力·对话 Talking about an AI Helper
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Lucy: My grandfather just got a small AI helper. It's amazing!
Tom: Really? What can it do for him?
Lucy: It reminds him to take his medicine and reads the news aloud.
Tom: That's so helpful. Does it ever make mistakes?
Lucy: Sometimes it hears the wrong word, and we all laugh.
Tom: Ha! Is your grandfather worried about it at all?
Lucy: A little. He says a machine must always be kept safe and private.
Tom: That's a wise point. New technology should help us, not control us.
exercises.translation_cn: Lucy 的爷爷有了个小型 AI 助手,很棒;它提醒爷爷吃药、朗读新闻;有时听错词逗大家笑;爷爷有点担心,说机器必须保证安全和隐私;Tom 赞同:新技术应帮助我们,而非控制我们。

questions.stem: Who got the AI helper?
What is one thing the AI helper does?
options: It reminds him to take his medicine.

questions.stem: Why do they sometimes laugh at the helper?
What is the grandfather a little worried about?
What do Lucy and Tom agree about technology?
options: It should help us, not control us.

exercises.title: U1 听力·短文 Tips for Writing a Sci-Fi Story
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Here are some simple tips for writing your own science fiction story.
First, think of one big idea, such as a robot, an alien, or a time machine.
Next, imagine how your world looks and how your machine works.
Then use vivid words to help readers picture the strange new sights.
Finally, leave a surprising ending so that readers keep thinking about your story.
exercises.translation_cn: 给你写科幻故事几个小贴士:先想一个大点子,比如机器人、外星人或时间机器;再想象你的世界长什么样、机器如何运转;然后用生动的词让读者在脑中描绘奇异的新景象;最后留一个出人意料的结尾,让读者回味无穷。

questions.stem: What should a writer think of first?
options: One big idea like a robot or time machine.

questions.stem: Why should a writer use vivid words?
